registry_info.name: vectors_demos
registry_info.description: Vector concept demonstration artifacts — applied physics demos showing vectors in action: force addition, work/energy, torque, reflection, and targeting.
registry_info.theoretical_grounding: Vector algebra, dot product (work, projection), cross product (torque, normals), force superposition, targeting and aiming algorithms

wedge_slide.name: Wedge Slide (inclined-plane free body)
wedge_slide.description: The inclined-plane free-body problem made playable - a primitive on a wedge, the force-decomposition toy for the embodied vectors-forces arc. A ToyConsole: the INCLINE slider sets the angle θ; the 3D demo shows the block on the slope with its force vectors (weight mg, normal N, friction f, and the net down-slope force); and the MONITOR draws the flat 2D free-body section - the textbook triangle with mg resolved into mg sinθ (down the slope) and mg cosθ (into it), N, friction, and the θ arc, auto-fit to the screen. Tilt past tan θ = μ and it goes from STATIC to SLIDING. mu is the (fixed) friction coefficient.

parameters.incline: 0..1 incline angle θ (12° to 55°) - past tan θ = μ the block slides (default 0.5)

force_mower.name: Force Mower (W = F d cos θ)
force_mower.description: The lawn-mower work diagram turned into a thing you push - an embodied force-display prop for the vectors-forces arc. Push the mower by its angled handle; the push F splits into the part that does work (F cos θ, along the ground) and the part wasted into the dirt (F sin θ, downward). The force vectors live on the object: F down the handle, the horizontal F cos θ, the green dashed vertical decomposition, the long purple displacement d, and a W = F d cos θ readout. DNA: push_angle 0..1 raises the handle angle θ so cos θ - the share of work - shrinks (steeper push, less work done).

parameters.push_angle: 0..1 handle/push angle θ (flat to steep) - cos θ shrinks the work (default 0.45)

force_cube.name: Force Cube (a vector you hold)
force_cube.description: A grabbable cube that draws the force you apply as an arrow out of its centre, split into x / y / z components - an embodied force-display prop. The cube IS the tail of the vector: wherever you push it the arrow points, and the three coloured component arrows (red Fx, green Fy, blue Fz) plus a dashed decomposition box show how one push is really three. A faint motion trail follows. DNA: push 0..1 is the force magnitude; seed sets its direction (live, both come from the grabbing hand's motion).

bubble_blaster.name: Bubble Blaster (output velocity vector)
bubble_blaster.description: A soap-bubble gun that fires a spreading cone of bubbles and wears its launch vector on the muzzle - an embodied force-display prop. Pull the trigger and bubbles pour out; the muzzle shows an arrow for the output velocity and a faint cone for the spread. Crank the output and the arrow stretches, the cone widens, the bubbles fly faster and further. Every emitter is a little vector field - each particle leaves with a velocity, and the spray's force is just that launch vector made of many departures. DNA: output 0..1 dials the launch (vector length, spread angle, bubble speed/count); seed jitters the bubbles.

parameters.output: 0..1 launch output - vector length, spread, bubble count (default 0.6)

vector_add.name: Vector Addition (a + b, two-pad console)
vector_add.description: Vector addition made playable - the entry operation of the embodied vectors-forces arc, a ToyConsole with a TWO-PAD control surface (synthesised from three interaction-design passes). Two 2D pads on the front lip, one per vector: drag a pad and that vector's tip follows your hand (a grabbed handle in VR, a pointer-drag on desktop). The two arrows draw head-to-tail on the console top and the resultant a+b swings live; the monitor shows the full component breakdown (a, b, a+b, |a+b|, angle). The control IS the vector tip. seed sets the starting a and b.

vector_sub.name: Vector Subtraction (a − b, two-pad console)
vector_sub.description: Vector subtraction made playable - the same two-pad ToyConsole as vector_add, flipped to a - b = a + (-b). Two 2D pads place the tips of a and b; the demo draws a, then the negated b head-to-tail, and the resultant a-b, with a faint ghost of the original +b so the flip reads as the whole idea. The monitor shows a, b, a-b, |a-b| and the angle. The control IS the vector tip; seed sets the starting a and b.

parameters.op: forced to sub by the scene

orbit_pair.name: Orbit Pair (gravity, F = G m₁m₂/r²)
orbit_pair.description: Gravity and orbits made playable - the clean rebuild of the old two-body sim, for the embodied vectors-forces arc. Two bodies pull on each other along the line between them, equal and opposite (Newton's third law), and orbit their shared centre of mass (the barycenter). Make one heavier and the barycenter slides toward it while the orbits resize - an equal binary becomes a star with a far-flung planet. Shows the two bodies on their dotted orbits, the equal-and-opposite gravity vectors, velocity tangents, the barycenter and the line of attraction, with an F = G m1m2/r^2 readout. DNA: mass_ratio 0..1 from a symmetric binary to a dominant star+planet; seed sets the orbital phase; color_a star, color_b planet, accent gravity vectors, orbit_color the paths.

parameters.mass_ratio: 0..1 from equal binary to dominant star+planet - shifts the barycenter and resizes the orbits (default 0.6)

circle_train.name: Circle Train (centripetal force, a = v²/r)
circle_train.description: Centripetal force made playable - a sci-fi intermezzo for the embodied vectors-forces arc. A high-speed neon maglev loop: the train's velocity is always tangent to the ring (grows with v) and its force always points inward toward the centre (grows with v^2/r). The payoff you can dial: double the speed and the inward force quadruples - the velocity arrow stretches linearly while the centripetal force arrow explodes. Glowing torus track, a banking train of cars, speed streaks, the tangent + inward vectors, and a v / a / F_c readout. DNA: speed 0..1 dials the train (velocity ~v linear, centripetal force ~v^2 quadratic); seed sets the train position; color_a neon track, color_b velocity, accent centripetal force, train_color the cars.

parameters.speed: 0..1 train speed - velocity grows linearly, centripetal force quadratically (default 0.7)

launch_arc.name: Launch Arc (projectile motion)
launch_arc.description: Projectile motion made playable - the launch / F=ma toy for the embodied vectors-forces arc (the pad that throws you). A launch pad fires at angle theta with speed v; gravity bends the straight launch vector into a parabola. The launch velocity decomposes into a horizontal vx (carries you) and a vertical vy (fights gravity); the trade between them sets the range = v^2 sin(2theta)/g - which peaks at 45 degrees. Shows the tilted glowing pad, the stroboscopic projectile arc, the launch vector + its vx/vy components, and apex / range markers. DNA: angle 0..1 sets the launch angle (flat to steep), power 0..1 the launch speed; color_a pad + components, color_b the arc + launch vector, accent pad glow + apex/range.

parameters.angle: 0..1 launch angle, flat to steep - range peaks at 45 deg (default 0.5)

drag_lane.name: Drag Lane (F = -b·v you feel)
drag_lane.description: Friction / drag made felt - a forces toy for the embodied vectors-forces arc. A runner enters a resistant medium at full tilt and slows under F = -b*v, so its velocity decays v ~ e^(-bt). Frozen stroboscopically, the runner's snapshots bunch together and its velocity arrows shrink as the drag eats the motion - run through air, water, honey and each pulls back harder. DNA: drag 0..1 sweeps from glide (snapshots evenly spread) to dead-stop (piled up fast); seed jitters the medium motes; color_a lane, color_b runner + velocity, accent drag particles, medium_color the resistant volume.

parameters.drag: 0..1 drag strength - sweeps the velocity decay from glide to dead-stop (default 0.5)

projection_shadow.name: Projection Shadow ((a·n̂)n̂ as a shadow)
projection_shadow.description: Vector projection made playable - the third operations toy with dot_aligner (dot) and torque_crank (cross). A sun overhead, an object floating off a rail; the object's shadow lands on the rail, and the shadow's distance from the origin IS a*n_hat - the projection of the object's position onto the axis n_hat. The perpendicular drop from object to shadow is the rejection (what doesn't live along n_hat). DNA: projection 0..1 swings the object from perpendicular (a perp n, no shadow) to along the rail (a parallel n, full shadow); seed jitters length; color_a rail/axis, color_b the vector a, accent the projection shadow, sun_color the light.

parameters.projection: 0..1 swings the object from perpendicular to along the rail - drives a*n_hat and the shadow length (default 0.7)

torque_crank.name: Torque Crank (r × F you can feel)
torque_crank.description: The cross product made playable - the operations pair to dot_aligner. A lever arm r and a push F meet at the hub of a flywheel; the torque tau = r x F = |r||F|sin(theta) points up the axle and spins the wheel. Force along the arm does nothing (sin 0); force across it spins hardest (sin 90). Shows r (cyan), F (orange), the tau torque axis (gold, up the axle), spin arrows and an rpm readout. DNA: leverage 0..1 sets the angle between r and F (0 = along the arm, 1 = perpendicular); seed jitters the arm bearing; color_a steel rig, color_b arm, force_color push, accent torque axis + flywheel glow.

parameters.leverage: 0..1 angle of the push F from the arm r - drives the torque sin(theta), the tau vector length and the spin (default 0.78)
parameters.accent: The torque axis tau + flywheel glow

dot_aligner.name: Dot-Aligner (aim · foe = mercy)
dot_aligner.description: The dot product made playable, and the embodied vectors-forces arc's operations toy. A swivel turret on a pedestal aims at a drifting foe-cube; the gold AIM vector (a) and the cyan DIRECTION-TO-FOE vector (b) meet at an angle, and a*b = cos(theta) is the charge. As alignment rises the angle closes, a lock BEAM ignites, and the foe converts FOE -> FRIEND (red -> green) - agreement here is mercy, not a kill. DNA: alignment 0..1 sets how locked the aim is (drives cos(theta), the beam, the conversion); seed jitters the foe bearing; color_a steel rig, color_b vectors, accent lock beam, foe_color/friend_color the conversion.

parameters.alignment: 0..1 how closely the aim points at the foe - drives cos(theta), the beam, and the conversion (default 0.78)

combined_forces_demo.name: Combined Forces Demo
combined_forces_demo.description: Vector addition as force combination — multiple forces acting on a body, visualized as arrows that add head-to-tail. The resultant force emerges from superposition.

work_energy_demo.name: Work-Energy Demo
work_energy_demo.description: Dot product as physical work — force dotted with displacement gives energy transfer. See why pushing perpendicular to motion does zero work.

torque_demo.name: Torque Demo
torque_demo.description: Cross product as torque — force applied at a lever arm produces rotation perpendicular to both. The right-hand rule determines which way things spin.

normal_force_demo.name: Normal Force & Reflection Demo
normal_force_demo.description: Vector projection and reflection — decompose velocity into normal and tangent components, then reflect. The math behind every bouncing ball and billiard shot.

turret_targeting.name: Turret Targeting
turret_targeting.description: Applied vector math for targeting — calculate direction, lead the target, account for projectile speed. Vectors solving the ancient problem of aiming at a moving target.

weather_vector_field.name: Weather Vector Field — Storm Chamber
weather_vector_field.description: A walkable storm chamber (~5x5 m) built on vector addition — two grabbable wind vectors combine in real-time. Drag arrow endpoints to feel how wind directions sum, then watch a real GPUParticles3D storm answer the resultant: rain streaks slant at the true gravity + wind angle, wind-blown debris streaks downwind (the vector in flight), drifting cloud slabs and swaying ground mist advect on the wind, and forked lightning strikes downwind in stormy weather. A MultiMesh field of arrows plus classic instruments — a yawing windsock, a spinning 3-cup anemometer, a ground compass rose, and fading streamlines — all read the same live summed vector. Four weather modes (calm / breezy / storm / blizzard) swap density, scale, colour, drift and lightning; calm adds a sun shaft with rising motes; blizzard turns the rain to slow white snow. Pressure zones distort the field; the ground tints warm/cool with the wind's vertical sign.

vector_reflection_demo.name: Vector Reflection Demo
vector_reflection_demo.description: Interactive vector reflection off a rotatable surface. An incoming vector (blue), surface normal (green), and reflected vector (red) update in real time as sliders control the surface angle and incoming direction. Demonstrates r = v - 2(v·n)n.

bounce_well.name: Bounce Well (restitution)
bounce_well.description: Restitution made playable - a console toy for the embodied vectors-forces arc (the clean rebuild of the bouncing-ball sim). A ball dropped into a well bounces, each bounce returning to e times the last height; frozen stroboscopically the arcs shrink geometrically. restitution 0..1 from a dead thud to a perpetual bounce.

parameters.demo_only: capture mode: drop the console, demo only

firework_burst.name: Firework Burst (projectile fountain)
firework_burst.description: The firework as pure projectile motion - a mortar throws sparks up in a cone and gravity arcs every one into a parabola. The console rebuild of the firework launcher. burst 0..1 from a tight low column to a wide high canopy of falling embers.

parameters.demo_only: capture mode: drop the console, demo only

momentum_cradle.name: Momentum Cradle (p = mv conserved)
momentum_cradle.description: Momentum conservation made playable - Newton's cradle, rebuilt as a console. Lift an end ball and the blow travels through the still middle balls untouched and kicks the far ball out to the same height: one in, one out, p = mv conserved. lift 0..1 sets the swing amplitude.

parameters.demo_only: capture mode: drop the console, demo only

slingshot_pull.name: Slingshot (elastic launch, PE = 1/2 k x^2)
slingshot_pull.description: The slingshot as stored energy - draw the pouch back and the band stores PE = 1/2 k x^2; release and it becomes launch speed, the projectile arcing away. The console rebuild of the slingshot launcher. draw 0..1; pull twice as far, store four times the energy.

parameters.draw: 0..1 draw distance (PE grows as draw squared)
parameters.demo_only: capture mode: drop the console, demo only

collision_carts.name: Collision Carts (momentum exchange)
collision_carts.description: Rigid-body collision made playable - a heavy cart meets a light one and momentum before equals momentum after, but the velocities split by mass. Shows the before and after lanes with carts sized by mass and their velocity vectors. The console rebuild of the rigid-body sim. mass_ratio 0..1 from a light striker to a heavy one.

parameters.demo_only: capture mode: drop the console, demo only

weather_vane.name: Weather Vane (wind ∝ v²)
weather_vane.description: Wind made playable - F_drag = ½ρv²C_dA. A ToyConsole: the WIND slider sets the speed; a weather vane swings to point downwind while a flag streams off the pole and the drag vector grows with the SQUARE of the speed - double the wind, quadruple the push, the flag snapping from a lazy ripple to horizontal. The clean toy the old wind-tunnel / windmill examples never became.

parameters.wind: 0..1 wind speed - the drag force climbs as v² (default 0.55)

pendulum_swing.name: Pendulum (T = 2π√(L/g))
pendulum_swing.description: The pendulum made playable - T = 2π√(L/g), restoring force = mg sin θ. A ToyConsole: the LENGTH slider sets L; the bob hangs at amplitude with gravity (down), tension (along the string) and the restoring component mg sin θ (along the swing), plus the swept arc. Lengthen the string and the swing slows by √L. The clean toy the old swinging-pendulum example never became.

spring_bob.name: Spring (F = −k x)
spring_bob.description: Hooke's law made playable - F = −kx, T = 2π√(m/k). A ToyConsole: the STIFFNESS slider sets k; a mass hangs on a coil where the spring force (+kx, up) balances the weight (down) at rest, and the stretch x is marked. Stiffen the spring and it barely gives - and it ticks faster, period shrinking as 1/√k. The clean toy the old spring-connection / mass-spring-damper examples never became.

parameters.stiffness: 0..1 spring stiffness k - less stretch, faster period as 1/√k (default 0.45)

lever_balance.name: Lever (τ = F·d)
lever_balance.description: The law of the lever made playable - τ = F·d, balanced when F₁d₁ = F₂d₂. A ToyConsole: the LOAD slider slides the right weight along the arm, changing its TORQUE (force times distance) not its weight; the beam tips toward the bigger torque and sits level only when the two are equal. A lever trades force for distance. The clean toy the old balance-puzzle / scale examples never became.

parameters.load: 0..1 load position along the arm - tips, balances, tips (default 0.5)

force_field_zone.name: Force Field Zone (a force made into a place)
force_field_zone.description: A 4 m cube of space where one vector replaces gravity. Throw a cube in - or step in yourself - and inside the field the only force is field_vector: point it down and everything falls into the void below; point it up-and-across and the same cube (and the same player) is carried to the far side. RigidBodies inside get gravity_scale 0 and velocity += field·dt; the player_body gets velocity += (field − its gravity)·dt. The wireframe cube, the grid of field-line arrows and the central vector show which way the world pushes. Driven by the vector_machine via group 'force_field'.

vector_machine.name: Vector Machine (the dial of gravity)
vector_machine.description: A console that aims and sizes the one vector ruling every force_field in the room. Three grabbable sliders - PITCH (down to up), YAW (which way across) and FORCE (how hard) - compose a single force vector, drawn live as a big arrow, and pushed straight into every force_field via set_field_vector(). The default is gravity: straight down, 9.8. Tilt it up-and-across and the void next door becomes a bridge.

parameters.force_max: max magnitude the FORCE slider reaches (default 15)

return_launcher.name: Return Launcher (the way home)
return_launcher.description: The catapult made sci-fi and made personal: instead of flinging a stone toward +Z it flings YOU on a ballistic arc back to where you started. Stand on the glowing launch ring and an energy arm snaps over; a velocity is solved on the spot - v0 = (home - here)/t - ½g·t - so that t seconds later you land exactly on your spawn. It can't throw the wrong way, because it always aims at the beginning (captured the first frame it sees the player). The final throw of a fly-up course. Fires the player's CharacterBody3D via an Area3D on the player layer, like force_pad.

parameters.flight_time: seconds of arc back to the start (default 3.0)

calder_mobile.name: Calder Mobile (balanced, real weights)
calder_mobile.description: A large hanging Calder mobile that is actually balanced. Every arm obeys the lever law τ = w·d: the two children of each rod are weighed, then the pivot is placed so w_left·d_left = w_right·d_right - the heavier shape rides the shorter arm - and the whole thing hangs level from a single ceiling point. Leaf masses are real: each flat painted disc is sheet aluminium, mass = π r²·t·ρ (t = 3 mm, ρ = 2700 kg/m³). Calder's primaries - red, yellow, blue, black, white. A plaque states the real total mass and the balance principle. Improves on the project's earlier calder_mobile_primaries, which was only a palette totem, not a balanced mobile.

calder_object_mobile.name: Calder Mobile (project primitives)
calder_object_mobile.description: The balanced Calder mobile (τ = w·d at every arm) but hung with the project's own ordinary objects - point, sphere, pyramid, arch - as the weights instead of painted discs. Each primitive carries a plausible mass and the arms balance those masses by the lever law, so the foundational shapes of the curriculum drift in equilibrium. A plaque states the total mass. Same CalderMobile script with use_objects = true.

pendulum_hall.name: Pendulum Hall (walk-in)
pendulum_hall.description: The body-scale, walk-in twin of pendulum_swing: a real, large pendulum (default L = 4.6 m) hung from a 6 m gantry, swinging live at its true period T = 2π√(L/g) = ~4.3 s. The restoring force mg sin θ hauls the bob back through bottom-dead-centre; a glowing arc on the floor records the swept path; the weight / tension / restoring vectors ride the bob at the scale of your own body. Stand in the hall and watch the giant bob pass. The large half of the 'intimate toy -> walk-in installation' pair (clusters with pendulum_swing).

parameters.arm_length: pendulum length L in m (default 4.6) - sets the period

centrifuge_ring.name: Centrifuge Ring (walk-in centripetal)
centrifuge_ring.description: The body-scale, walk-in twin of circle_train: a pod laps a big neon ring while the velocity (tangent) and centripetal force (inward, ∝ v²/r) ride it at your own scale. Velocity is always tangent, the force always toward the centre you never reach; crank the speed and the inward arrow explodes as the square. a = v²/r made into a ridden loop you stand inside.

spring_tower.name: Spring Tower (walk-in Hooke)
spring_tower.description: The body-scale, walk-in twin of spring_bob: a heavy mass bobs on a giant coil at its real period T = 2π√(m/k); the coil stretches and compresses while the spring force (−kx) and the weight trade places at body scale. F = −kx, the signature of everything that keeps time. Stand beside the tower and watch it tick.

orbit_walk.name: Orbit Walk (walk-in two-body)
orbit_walk.description: The body-scale, walk-in twin of orbit_pair: stand at the barycenter while a heavy star and a lighter planet wheel around you on opposite sides, the equal-and-opposite gravity vectors (F = G m1 m2 / r squared) riding each body. Make one heavier and the barycenter slides toward it, the orbits resizing to keep the balance. An orbit is two things falling toward each other and missing, around a centre that belongs to neither.

parameters.mass_ratio: 0..1 — heavier star slides the barycenter toward it

drag_corridor.name: Drag Corridor (walk-in air/water/honey)
drag_corridor.description: The body-scale, walk-in twin of drag_lane: a corridor of three media (air, water, honey) you walk through, your own pace damped more in each denser section. A probe in each zone glides and dies under F = -b*v, its velocity arrow shrinking as it bunches up — the same launch goes far in air, less in water, barely a lunge in honey. Drag is the world charging you rent on speed.

work_meter.name: Work Meter (W = F·d·cosθ)
work_meter.description: The intimate companion to force_mower for Work: a block on a rail and a force applied at an angle theta, so only the along-the-ground part (F cos theta, green) does work while the perpendicular part (F sin theta) is wasted. Raise the angle and the work falls even though you push just as hard. The world only feels the part of a force that goes its way.

parameters.angle: 0..80 degrees of the applied force above the ground

free_vector.name: Free Vector (direction + length)
free_vector.description: The intimate companion to VectorBasics for Vector basics: one arrow and its ghost copies, carried to different origins to show a vector has no home. A vector is two facts only - a direction and a length; slide it anywhere and it is the same vector. A vector is a journey with no starting address.

coordinate_locator.name: Coordinate Locator (applied coordinates)
coordinate_locator.description: Applied coordinate system: a beacon locates a real point by reading off its (x, y, z) address, dropping dashed lines to each axis the way GPS pins you to the grid. Space is a promise three numbers keep.

route_vector.name: Route Vector (applied displacement)
route_vector.description: Applied vector basics: a from-pin and a to-pin, and the one arrow between them is the displacement - the trip, not the places. A courier walks the arrow. A vector is a journey with no starting address.

tug_of_war.name: Tug of War (applied addition)
tug_of_war.description: Applied vector addition: two ropes pull one load from different angles and it moves along their sum, not either rope alone. Change an angle and the resultant swings. Forces add by walking, not by counting.

river_crossing.name: River Crossing (applied subtraction)
river_crossing.description: Applied vector subtraction: a boat crossing a flowing river aims upstream so heading = target - current, and lands true. Relative velocity is the gap between the course you steer and the course you make.

throttle_gain.name: Throttle Gain (applied scaling)
throttle_gain.description: Applied scalar multiplication: a throttle multiplies a base thrust by a factor k, growing the arrow along its own axis without turning it. A scalar is a volume knob for a direction.

brake_skid.name: Brake Skid (applied friction)
brake_skid.description: Applied friction: a sled flung across the ground skids to a stop, the braking force dragging against its motion and laying down skid marks. Distance = v squared / (2 mu g). Friction is the world's brake.

magnitude_bench.name: Magnitude Bench (|v| = sqrt(x2+y2+z2))
magnitude_bench.description: Bench-scale magnitude: a tabletop vector whose x, y, z component edges build the box whose space diagonal is its length. |v| = sqrt(x2+y2+z2), read live as the components breathe.

torque_bench.name: Torque Bench (tau = |r||F| sin th)
torque_bench.description: Bench-scale torque: a lever on a pivot and a force at its end; push along the arm and nothing turns, push across it and it spins hardest. Only the perpendicular part makes torque. tau = |r||F| sin theta.

centripetal_bench.name: Centripetal Bench (a = v2/r)
centripetal_bench.description: Bench-scale centripetal: a tabletop turntable, a mass circling a hub, velocity tangent and force inward. a = v2/r - the inward arrow is the only thing bending the straight line into a circle.

restitution_bench.name: Restitution Bench (h' = e h)
restitution_bench.description: Bench-scale restitution: a strobe of one ball's bounces, each peak a fixed fraction of the last, with a live ball hopping through them. h' = e*h - the coefficient of restitution is the tax on every fall.

newton_bench.name: Newton Bench (F = m a)
newton_bench.description: Bench-scale Newton's second law: a mass on a table, a force pushing it, the acceleration it produces. a = F/m, dialed live. The cleanest statement of what a force does.

velocity_bench.name: Velocity Bench (v = vx + vy)
velocity_bench.description: Bench-scale velocity: a puck crossing a table with its velocity drawn and split into the part that carries it across (vx) and the part that lifts it (vy). Motion is a vector the world keeps editing.

wind_toy.name: Wind Toy (held vane)
wind_toy.description: The small, held end of Wind: a pinwheel on a stick and a streamer that leans - the least you need to feel a force you cannot see. F drag grows with v squared, so it spins faster and the streamer flattens as the breeze rises. You never see the wind, only the bend of the things it pushes.

wind_bench.name: Wind Bench (fan + windsock)
wind_bench.description: The bench-scale middle of Wind: a desk fan and a windsock, the push made readable as the sock swings from hanging to horizontal. F = half rho v squared Cd A grows with the square of speed. Wind is air with somewhere to be; the force is in the speed, squared.

wind_room.name: Wind Room (walk-in field)
wind_room.description: The room-scale, walk-in end of Wind: a field of tall windsocks you stand among, all leaning the same way, so the invisible field becomes a place. A wind field is one direction and one speed filling the space. Wind is a force that has decided to be everywhere at once - and you are in it.

work_toy.name: Work Toy (held W = F.d.cos th)
work_toy.description: Hand-scale Work: a small block pushed a short distance at an angle; the useful along-the-ground part does work, the perpendicular part is wasted. The world only feels the part of a force that goes its way.

work_room.name: Work Room (walk-in F.d)
work_room.description: Room-scale Work: push a big cart down a long floor and watch the work accumulate as force paid out over distance. Only the part along the motion counts.

lever_toy.name: Lever Toy (held seesaw)
lever_toy.description: Hand-scale lever: a beam on a fulcrum with a weight each side; it tips toward the larger moment and settles. tau = F.d; a lever trades force for distance.

lever_room.name: Lever Room (walk-in balance beam)
lever_room.description: Room-scale lever: a big balance beam on a tall fulcrum, heavy near the pivot vs light far out, settling at F1.d1 = F2.d2. Far out, a small weight outweighs a big one near in.

vector_bench.name: Vector Bench (direction + length)
vector_bench.description: Bench-scale vector basics: an arrow that sweeps both its direction and its length, with its components drawn. A vector is two facts only - a direction and a length.

scaling_bench.name: Scaling Bench (k x v)
scaling_bench.description: Bench-scale scaling: a base vector and an output = k.v that grows and shrinks along the same line as the dial turns. A scalar is a volume knob for a direction.

field_bench.name: Field Bench (a vector at every point)
field_bench.description: Bench-scale force field: a grid of little arrows all pointing one slowly-rotating direction, with a test dot drifting in the field. A field is force that has decided to be everywhere at once.

magnitude_hall.name: Magnitude Hall (walk-in |v|)
magnitude_hall.description: Room-scale magnitude: a giant vector spanning the floor with its component box as walkable dashed edges; walk the diagonal and read |v| = sqrt(x2+y2+z2).

force_room.name: Force Room (walk-in F = m.a)
force_room.description: Room-scale Newton's second law: a big mass with an applied force arrow and the acceleration it produces, a = F/m at body scale. A force is a vector applied to a mass.

projection_toy.name: Projection Toy (held, onto a line)
projection_toy.description: Hand-scale projection: a vector and a rail; the shadow of the vector along the rail is the projection (v.n_hat), the perpendicular drop is the rejection. Projection is the part of you that lives along someone else's line.
